classification_rationale: I8/E3 derives LOW, NICE. (1) 'The rig relaxes what a deployment must not' lists 'an agent-to-gateway edge with one-way TLS, where the gateway does not verify agent client certificates'; that is the shipped reference production shape (origin/dev deploy/docker/reference-gateway-sys.config agent listener verify_none / fail_if_no_peer_cert false so CSR enrolment completes; docker-compose.reference-gateway.yml header: 'agent<->gateway is one-way TLS'), so the 'must not' framing is wrong for that item and could lead a reader to require client certificates on :50051, which the routed gateway row warns breaks agent bootstrap. (2) 'no monitoring, persistence or hardening' is not accurate: the rig has named volumes certs, server-data, postgres-data that persist across `down` (the compose header says never `down -v` casually) and ca-export is read_only with cap_drop ALL; what it lacks is backups, a restart policy (restart: no), and a monitoring stack. (3) Not listed, and material to the same reader: a multi-use enrolment token (max_uses 100000, ttl 72 h) that mints agent certificates, an unauthenticated HAProxy stats and Prometheus endpoint on :8404 reachable from every agent on the bridge, agent data dirs on tmpfs mode 0777, and that docker access (used for every fault sidecar with NET_ADMIN) is root-equivalent, which sits beside the unchanged 'no host root' text at record L52 and script header L28. (4) The script header does not carry the caveat the compose header does (the original finding named both).
summary: Reword the bullet as 'among other things' and fix (1) and (2); add the token, stats port, 0777 tmpfs and docker-access items; qualify 'no host root' as 'no sudo, but docker access is root-equivalent'; add one line to the script header. Not blocking.

trigger: the server container stops (restart: no) after load_state resolved the REST port, and another local process binds that now-free ephemeral port before the next curl
classification_rationale: I9/E5 derives INFO, NICE. need_rest guards the value resolved at the last load_state, not the moment of the send. The URL is resolved once and reused: in `up` the login follows up to ~7 minutes of waits (REST wait 120 s plus three /readyz waits of up to 90 s), in `mgmt` a wait of up to 120 s, and in `scenario` dispatch_probe reuses the scenario-start value for 400 s or more. In the dispatch_probe case only the session cookie (not the password) would be sent. The exposure also requires a same-host attacker, who can already read the same throwaway password from ps and docker inspect, so nothing is gained; kept as a record of the residual after the stale-port fix, not as a defect to act on. Related robustness note: after a recreate, wait_for expands $SPIKE_SERVER_URL once, so a transiently empty lookup is never retried and cmd_mgmt waits out 120 s before need_rest dies.
summary: Optional: re-run load_state (or a cheap `compose port`) immediately before each login. Not needed for a throwaway local rig.
